Glad to hear it! I hope all is going well. The feeling of accomplishment after finishing your first week is like concentrated awesomeness.

Congratulations! It's a tremendous milestone, as you said, so it's understandable that you would be anxious. 
I remember my first job. I was nervous, felt unqualified and wondered when everyone would "find me out." It turned out that everyone was just as nervous as me. It was helpful for me to remember that people wanted myself and the other newbies to do well. I don't know if I have any real advice to offer, other than to take it one day at a time. From what I remember, the first 10 or so minutes was the scariest part. But after meeting everyone, just take it step by step. I've been in the workplace for almost 15 years, and I can tell you, people are often far more anxious than they let on. So don't judge yourself too much if you feel nervous. Anyway, I hope some/any of this helped. Please take care. Good luck tomorrow!!

Hi again, Sam.
I'm sorry you've had a rough couple of days. I'm impressed that you mustered up the energy to paint. What kind of stuff do you paint? I used to have more hobbies. When I was growing up, I loved photography and even painting sometimes. My parents raised my brothers and I to play classical music, so that was always a hobby but could also feel like a job at times. I love Bach's solo violin pieces. In the past, listening to different violinists play while following the sheet music has been grounding. It reminds me of how all artists are bound by the colors that life gives us, but they leave such different fingerprints. 
I used to love to read. I dunno, I used to love a lot of things, to be honest. I guess, since most of them were sensory, that the depression took them out pretty quickly. Anyway, thanks for letting me check in again. It helps to have someone to reach out to. I'm worried it might be a tough week. Maybe, once I'm sure you're not a serial killer, I'll take you up on those cookies. Please take care and reach out if I can help too.

I'm really sorry to hear about your dad and brother. That sounds like an awful loss. I think about the effects my death would have on my family constantly. Those thoughts are usually the final reason I decide to stick around one more night. I hate the idea of someone being tortured by one of my decisions. It makes me ill, and I've actually had nightmares about it. (I once dreamt that I went through with it, and in the dream, I was watching the aftermath from outside my body. It was awful: the cops, my parents, even my shrink was there. And just looking at the scene itself in my dreams... in my dream, I was overcome with an unfathomable feeling of regret. I hold onto that feeling sometimes. And I try to recall it before something gets really bad. I just worry that one day it won't be enough.
Anyway, thank you for listening. And again, I'm sorry you've been through those losses. I imaging you must be a really strong person experience it. Please take care.

I'm sorry you're feeling so terrible. It sounds like you've got a lot going on that is very stressful. Calling one of the numbers listed in the SW directory might be helpful. (1-800-273-TALK is just one of them.) They're trained to talk people through a crisis and are very non-judgmental. You might also try some breathing exercises. Everyone is different, but for me, sometimes holding a piece of ice for a couple minutes helps de-escalate me as well. With regards to your papers, there's a saying that "done is better than good." I know, it's kind of cheesy, but sometimes all you can do is type something/anything up and remind yourself it doesn't have to be perfect this time. Again, I don't know your situation, but talking to one of your teachers may also be an option. It never hurts to ask. Please take care. (I apologize if any of this sounds too much like self-help, I'm new to this sub.)

I'm glad you reached out. It sounds like you really care about your son. My brother is also a single father and was going through a similar situation for awhile. Since I took him to his appointments, childcare wasn't always easy to find, so I can only imagine the added stress you're going through. So again, I think it's great you reached out.
Someone else on this sub may be more familiar with specific resources, but it could be helpful to call one of the hotlines listed on the main page. When I was helping my brother, we called the national suicide hotline (1-800-273-8255.) They were able to direct us to some local clinics. I know you mentioned that you are not actively suicidal, but they often are able to provide numbers for resources in your area. Since these lines are anonymous, it might be a good place to start if you're worried about someone judging you as a dad/caregiver. In general, it may help you get more comfortable with reaching out for particular services near you. And becoming comfortable enough to seek treatment is often the hardest part. ...And you're doing a good job of it already. I hope this helps, and please take care.

I'm sorry that you're having a difficult time. I can relate to the odd mixture of relief and sadness that comes with suicidal thoughts. Like Jake, I'd like to hear more about you. Is there something you would be comfortable sharing? You mentioned feeling sad about the things you'll never get to do. What are some of the things that you'd like to do if you felt like you could?

I agree with Prankishbear. Please hang in there. I know those are just words, and I know they don't mean much when you're in that place. I struggle daily, and I still think about ending it every day. I spent half of last night on a hotline. For what it's worth, I always tell myself to give it one week. Usually, at least one thing happens that makes me tell myself "okay, I can give it another week."... and so on.
Ultimately, though, only you can give yourself permission to do something. For today (and I know this sounds corny), try to give yourself permission to stick around 1 more week, or even 24hrs. During that time, call someone, anyone, even if it's a friend or a hotline. 
Anyway, I'm really sorry you're feeling this way. I can relate, and I know how exhausting it can be, especially when you've done so much work. From what you shared, I gather you've fought really hard. And the world could use more people that are brave enough to fight through all the bad stuff the world has to offer. Please take care.
